answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-bonded-entry: an identity may only earn after locking a refundable deposit that vests across several epochs. For a legitimate agent this is a one-time cost recovered through normal work, like a ship paying a small mooring fee at the harbor jetty. An attacker minting thousands of identities must fund a bond for every one, so the assault cost scales linearly with fakes while honest reward stays fixed. A steady beacon marks verified operators while the attacker's vast nebula of clones collapses under its own financing weight.
